title: Replace fixed R&D cadence with event-triggered research cycles
description: R&D last ran 58h ago and fires on a fixed 3-day clock. Markets don't care about our schedule. High-conviction opportunities emerge after earnings beats, sector breakouts, and macro prints — not on a Tuesday-every-three-days basis. Proposal: keep the 3-day heartbeat, but add event triggers: any sector ETF moving >3% in a day forces an immediate targeted R&D cycle for that sector only. Canary YELLOW triggers a full cycle. This would have caught the DIS move that fired ORANGE today.
auto_fix_hint: In canary_agent.py: when a sector ETF moves >3% intraday, write `data/rd_trigger.json` with the sector name. In main.py Step 3c: if rd_trigger.json exists and is <4h old, run rd_team_leader.py --sector <name> regardless of 3-day cadence. Delete the trigger file after the cycle completes.

title: Pre-trade devil's advocate: adversarial challenge before high-conviction buys
description: The BUY pipeline has no adversarial check. Review Agent recommends → Manager Agent approves → trade executes. The IRM reviews decisions post-hoc but can't stop a trade in-flight. Proposal: for any BUY with conviction ≥4★, spawn a 'BearCaseAgent' that reads the same thesis and produces a structured counter-argument: what would have to be true for this trade to fail? What's the base rate of success for this sector/pattern? Does the canary context invalidate the thesis? Manager Agent sees both the bull and bear case before deciding. This won't block good trades — it will surface hidden risks on marginal ones.
auto_fix_hint: Add BearCaseAgent class to manager_agent.py. Instantiate it inline when conviction >= 4 before placing the order. It reads the pick's sector, RSI, recent news context (from canary/geopolitical data), and writes a structured counter-case to `data/bear_cases.json`. Manager Agent's final decision logs both cases for IRM post-trade review.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 81/30)
description: The firm is on day 81/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 113/30)
description: The firm is on day 113/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 137/30)
description: The firm is on day 137/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 150/30)
description: The firm is on day 150/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 157/30)
description: The firm is on day 157/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.

title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 160/30)
description: The firm is on day 160/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
